svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A phagocyte and a bacterium. Chemicals from the bacterium attract the phagocyte (chemotaxis)."], [1, "The phagocyte moves towards the bacterium."], [3.5, "Pseudopodia flow around the bacterium."], [5.5, "The pseudopodia fuse, enclosing the bacterium in a vesicle: a phagosome."], [8.5, "Lysosomes move to the phagosome and fuse with it: a phagolysosome."], [10.5, "Hydrolytic enzymes digest the bacterium."], [14, "Useful products are absorbed; indigestible debris is released by exocytosis."]]
svg.title: Phagocytosis
svg.desc: A neutrophil moves towards a bacterium, surrounds it with pseudopodia, encloses it in a phagosome, lysosomes fuse and their enzymes digest it, and debris is released.
svg.text: A neutrophil engulfing a bacterium (not to scale).

g.data-info: A white blood cell that engulfs and digests pathogens. Neutrophils have a lobed nucleus.
Extensions of the cell surface membrane that flow around the pathogen.
Typical of neutrophils; helps them squeeze through capillary walls.
Vesicles of hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes made by the Golgi apparatus.
Chemicals it releases attract the phagocyte (chemotaxis).
